## Description

A social amoeba of forest soil (~10 µm). With bacteria it eats and divides (~4 h per generation).
Starved, within hours it becomes competent: some cells fire cAMP pulses every ~6 min, neighbours
relay them (release their own pulse and stay refractory for minutes) and move towards the wave front;
spiral or concentric waves gather the cells into streams towards a centre.

## In the simulation

<!-- GENERATED:presence -->
Drops: `pond` (weight 0.15), `puddle` (weight 0.15); 12 individuals in a reference drop at weight 1.
<!-- /GENERATED -->

[cAMP relay and chemotaxis](../../mechanics/chemical-signals.md#camp-relay-dictyostelium): competence after
starvation, pacemakers, threshold relay, refractory period, and climbing the gradient while the
signal rises. cAMP diffuses with D ≈ 400 µm²/s and is degraded in ~1 min by phosphodiesterase; it
uses `bio_time` so the wave has its real length. Migration in biological time (~15 µm/min). Simulated
up to the aggregation streams. Threshold, pulse and pacemaker fraction are orders of magnitude.

## Literature

- Konijn T.M. et al. (1967) (cAMP as the acrasin).
- Tomchik K.J., Devreotes P.N. (1981) Science 212: 443 (cAMP waves).
- Martiel J.-L., Goldbeter A. (1987) Biophys. J. 52: 807 (relay model).
- Dworkin M., Keller K.H. (1977) (cAMP diffusion coefficient).
- Sussman M. (1987) Methods Cell Biol. 28: 9–29 (~4 h generation on bacteria at 22 °C; to verify).

## Not implemented yet

- The mound, slug and fruiting body are multicellular and are not simulated.
- No phosphodiesterase secretion as a separate field; no cell-type differentiation (prestalk,
  prespore).

## Unique and shared mechanics

The only being with [signal relay](../../mechanics/chemical-signals.md); shares the
[plastic membrane](../../mechanics/soft-bodies.md) and phagocytosis with the other amoebae.
